questions.q: Why do mass transactions exist rather than requiring every asset to be processed individually?
options: Because individual transactions are not supported at all
Because mass transactions are required for all new asset additions
Because individual transactions do not calculate gain or loss
Because many real-world events affect many assets at once, and processing them individually is slow and risks inconsistency
questions.explain: Events like a warehouse closure or product discontinuation affect many assets simultaneously; mass transactions apply the same treatment consistently and efficiently.

questions.q: Which mass transaction type moves a group of assets to a new location or distribution?
options: Mass Retirements
Mass Transfers
Mass Reclassifications
Mass Changes
questions.explain: Mass Transfers apply Lesson 23's transfer logic (location, assignment, distribution) to a selected group of assets in one operation.

questions.q: What does Mass Changes specifically update?
options: An individual asset's retirement date
The General Ledger's accounting calendar
A single asset's assigned employee
Category-level defaults, optionally applied retroactively to existing assets in that category
questions.explain: Mass Changes updates category-level defaults (life, method, accounts) and can optionally apply that change retroactively to assets already in the category.

questions.q: How does a mass transaction determine which assets it will affect?
options: It always affects every asset in the entire book
By randomly sampling a subset of assets
Only assets added in the current period are eligible
Through selection criteria (category, location, cost center, date range) that builds a candidate list for review
questions.explain: A mass transaction uses selection criteria to filter and build a candidate list, which is reviewed before the transaction commits.

questions.q: Why does review of the candidate list matter especially for mass transactions?
options: Because mass transactions cannot be reviewed before submission
Because mass transactions never affect gain or loss calculations
Because review is only required for retirements, not transfers
Because a mistake in the selection criteria is multiplied across every asset that matched it
questions.explain: Since a mass transaction affects every asset matching its selection criteria, a poorly specified filter can incorrectly include or exclude many assets at once, making careful review essential.
